summary: Radar for 2026-11-22, GLP-1 focus, 4 days before US Thanksgiving. Three things stand out. (1) The holiday table is at its peak. PBS and US News both ran "feasting on a GLP-1" guides on 11-20 and 11-21, and our "still full the morning after" Short got 504 views on day 1, so the 20:00 holiday Shorts should keep pointing to Thanksgiving through 11-27. (2) Foundayo is the best window for a long video with a searched drug name. The TGA registered it on 11-16, it is reaching Australian pharmacies now, the Wegovy pill launched in Australia the same week, and our Foundayo nausea Short got 826 views on day 1. Ship the held Foundayo what-to-expect long video as soon as the 11-22 render fixes clear, then follow with a label-only "pill vs injection" explainer. (3) The FDA's class-wide NAION eye warning is still spreading through follow-on coverage: a baseline-exam Q&A in Ophthalmology Times, Denmark paying compensation in 31 cases, law-firm pieces, and News-Medical on 11-19. That fits the label-change format, and the right way in is the Serious Risks re-render (6 vs 4 per 100,000 a year, plus same-day care for sudden painless vision loss). Muscle is the next broad long video. The T-REx RCT is being picked up by MarketWatch, the Washington Post and SMH ("lost 10 kg of muscle"), which suits "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Muscle Loss: How Much in the Trials?". The broad weight-variability question ("why doesn't it work the same for everyone") is getting news pickup, but the ScienceDaily piece is a commentary on an ongoing observational study, so the trial distribution has to carry it. Retatrutide's NEJM knee-pain trials (TRIUMPH-4) are the only fresh randomized result with a searched name, but the drug is unapproved and peptide black-market stories are circulating. Caution, label it investigational, and don't use a "What is" format. Rejected: the compounded tirzepatide price comparison, the CBP counterfeit and peptide-import stories, observational cancer and pancreatitis signals as topics, and the TiTRE titration protocol.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) muscle loss: how much in the trials, and what the T-REx randomized trial says about lifting weights
candidates.angle: A broad searched question with a hopeful payoff. About 25% of the weight lost was lean mass in the 160-person DXA substudy (the 75/25 split), and in T-REx, weight training with tirzepatide meant less lean-mass loss and more strength for similar weight loss. Answer the SMH '10 kg of muscle' fear with the trial numbers and two first steps (protein, resistance training). Link to Strength after 11-24.
